subject: Energy
title: Land Use and Energy
description: A short lesson to help you apply Land Use and Energy.

hook.text: All energy sources use land—but the amount varies enormously, from dense nuclear plants to sprawling solar farms.

buildup.text: A nuclear plant produces 1 GW on roughly 1 km²—a solar farm needs about 20 km² for the same annual output.

discovery.text: Wind farms use vast areas but share land with farming—cattle graze and crops grow between turbines.

twist.text: Rooftop solar uses no new land at all—turning existing buildings into power plants with zero additional land footprint.

climax.text: Agrivoltaics (solar panels above crops) boost land productivity—shade-tolerant crops actually yield more under panels.

punchline.text: Dense or sprawling—every energy source has a land cost.

quiz.question: What is agrivoltaics?
options: Solar panels above crops, sharing land
